I'm trying to use d3 to draw a network graph. And my origin dataset is like this(json):

```
{

        }

            "target": "00R",
            "opacity": 0.61
        }

}
```

And through this, I can code like below to generate a network graph **with given nodes and links:**
```
d3.json("./air.json",` function( data) {
        var link = svg
        .attr("class","links")
            .selectAll("line")
            .data(data.links)
            .enter()
            .append("line")
            .style("stroke", "#000000")
            .style("stroke-width",1)
   
        var node = svg
            .selectAll("circle")
            .data(data.nodes)
            .enter()
            .append("circle")
            .attr("r", 1)
            .style("fill", "#000000")


        var simulation = d3.forceSimulation(data.nodes)                 
            .force("link", d3.forceLink()                               
                    .id(function(d) { return d.id; })                     
                    .links(data.links)                                    
            )
            .force("charge", d3.forceManyBody().strength(-400))         
            .force("center", d3.forceCenter(width / 2, height / 2))     
            .on("end", ticked);

        function ticked() {
            link
                .attr("x1", function(d) { return d.source.x; })
                .attr("y1", function(d) { return d.source.y; })
                .attr("x2", function(d) { return d.target.x; })
                .attr("y2", function(d) { return d.target.y; })
                .style("opacity",function(d) {return (Math.sqrt((d.source.x-d.target.x)*(d.source.x-d.target.x)+(d.source.y-d.target.y)))/1200; });
                // (Math.sqrt((d.source.x-d.target.x)*(d.source.x-d.target.x)+(d.source.y-d.target.y)))/300
            node
                .attr("cx", function (d) { return d.x; })
                .attr("cy", function(d) { return d.y; });
        }
```

It appears I cannot use [react-select](https://github.com/JedWatson/react-select) and d3-zoom at the same time.

(EDIT: Please see the updated codesandbox: https://codesandbox.io/s/xenodochial-mccarthy-sjqv8w?file=/src/App.js and comment out Select on line 61 to see the behavior, rather what is described in the following quote)

> https://codesandbox.io/s/wizardly-noyce-zoyndj?file=/src/App.js
> 
> In the above code sandbox, as-is, I cannot reliably zoom and choose a select option.

> 
> If I instead comment out `initZoom()` on line 52 (to disable the zoom behavior), the svg shows up and the select works.
> 

I honestly suspect this is more a problem with react-select than with d3-zoom, but the one thing that gives me pause regarding that theory is that I was able to use react-select and cytoscapejs at the same time, with similar mouse-driven zooming features.

I filed a [companion bug](https://github.com/JedWatson/react-select/issues/5479) with react-select. There is also an open [stackoverflow question](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/74418763/why-do-react-select-and-d3-zoom-conflict) in case someone can find a workaround.
